results.primary_cause: No accessible time-consistent external evidence was found confirming the current BDI/Capesize/Panamax and commodity-volume freight cycle. Price-based evidence is excluded.
No accessible time-consistent external evidence was found confirming the current container spot or contract freight cycle and liner utilization. Price-based evidence is excluded.

Available nuclear evidence was related to uranium production or general SMR deployment, not time-consistent nuclear-specific buildout generating second-order demand for grid equipment. The exact causal link remains unconfirmed.

Evidence of elevated electricity demand was found, but no accessible time-consistent primary or high-quality source confirmed power-electronics or power-equipment capital expenditure, orders, or backlog. Demand evidence alone is insufficient for this exact driver.

Supermicro reported record AI/IT infrastructure demand, more than $60 billion in new orders, record backlog entering fiscal 2027, and fiscal 2026 net sales of $39.1 billion versus $22.0 billion a year earlier. This confirms an active AI-server/infrastructure shipment and backlog cycle at the company level, but does not establish industry-wide ODM breadth.

supporting_evidence.claim: Supermicro reported more than $60 billion in new orders, record backlog entering fiscal 2027, accelerating demand, and fiscal 2026 net sales of $39.1 billion versus $22.0 billion in fiscal 2025.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Supermicro Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results

counter_evidence.claim: Supermicro disclosed that its financial results were preliminary and that an independent review of certain transactions related to export-control issues could affect forecasts and reported results.
counter_evidence.source_title: Supermicro Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results
